A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfiniteWeb and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices A-F. Corresponding methods, experiments, and appendix material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original website-generation evaluations, agent-training results, ablations, execution-trace analyses, and human verification studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds MobileWorld results and a controlled comparison of training-data generators.

M1.justification: The four-stage synthesis pipeline, TCTDD procedure, dense-reward evaluators, and Appendix F prompts are unchanged. Appendix C.4's discussion of context management explains the existing procedure without establishing a method modification.

E1.justification: MobileWorld adds a distinct mobile GUI evaluation domain, extending demonstrated transfer beyond web and desktop tasks (Sections 4.1 and 4.4; Table 9). The earlier benchmarks and synthetic training-task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 adds training on Claude-Code-generated websites as a comparator for downstream agent performance. Claude-Code previously participated in website-quality comparisons, but this training-source comparison is new. Earlier comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new training-source comparison holds the 600-task GRPO setup and GPT-5/high generation configuration constant across generators. MobileWorld is evaluated without additional fine-tuning. Previously stated generation and training settings in Appendix B are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a focused analysis of training-data quality versus task quantity, including a website page-count comparison. The TCTDD, backbone, and dense-reward ablations, generated-environment difficulty analysis, and Appendix A case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three-run averages, standard deviations, and Welch's t-tests are unchanged. The new comparison also averages three runs, continuing the established practice without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New results include MobileWorld baseline/Claude-Code-trained/InfiniteWeb-trained scores of 6.4%/5.1%/10.3%, and Claude-Code-trained Online-Mind2Web/OSWorld scores of 23.7%/25.2% (Table 9). These substantially extend the transfer and training-source evidence. Page-count and parallel-generation measurements are also added; earlier benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The existing reward-checkpoint calculation and training formulation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary extend the performance claim to MobileWorld and explicitly emphasize cross-platform transferability. The central claims about scalable environment synthesis, functional correctness, and visual quality remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 attributes the training advantage to data quality and context management. The limitations now distinguish demonstrated mobile transfer from unsupported native-mobile environment generation, discuss cross-application transfer despite single-website training, and contextualize generation cost and overhead.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a repository link and states that code and generated websites are publicly available. v3 newly reports approximately 125 minutes for parallel generation of 600 websites and a 6.9% share of total training time. Existing prompts and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds MobileWorld and UI-Evol citations and briefly positions UI-Evol within synthetic-data research. Design2Code and Generative UI reference updates correspond to already cited works, rather than additional research contributions.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and spelling corrections, updates title/contact text, adds subsection C.4, and expands the limitations. The main section sequence, method exposition, and extensive prompt appendix remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the website showcase in Figure 2 and the training-source comparison in Table 9. It moves the scaling plot from v1 Figure 5 to v3 Figure 1 and reflows existing material. The retained diagrams, plots, case-study displays, and prompt boxes are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: MobileWorld evaluation and the matched 600-task training-source control strengthen evidence for transfer and the value of InfiniteWeb-generated data. Access information and quantified generation overhead also help. The improvement is limited by sparse MobileWorld-specific evaluation details and a context-management explanation that the new control does not isolate experimentally.
